flashcard_questions.q: What did the miasma theory claim caused disease?
flashcard_questions.a: Bad air or foul smells rising from rotting matter

flashcard_questions.q: Which ancient Greek theory of four body liquids still survived in the 18th century?
What name was given to practitioners who combined haircutting with tooth-pulling and bloodletting?
Which practitioners prepared and sold medicines, acting as forerunners of modern pharmacists?
What name was given to travelling salesmen who sold fake cure-all medicines?
Which imported medicine from South American tree bark was used to treat malaria?
What was the belief that a monarch's touch could cure scrofula called?
Which movement of the 17th and 18th centuries put reason and science above tradition?
Which surgeon is known as the 'Father of Scientific Surgery'?
How did John Hunter treat a popliteal aneurysm instead of amputating the leg?
flashcard_questions.a: He tied off the artery higher up the leg

flashcard_questions.q: How many hanged criminals a year had Henry VIII granted surgeons for dissection?
What name was given to men who stole fresh corpses from graves to sell to surgeons?
What year did surgeons break away from the barbers to form the Company of Surgeons?
Which professional body, established in 1800, oversees surgery in England?
What new institutions gave the poor medicine and advice without paying for a doctor's visit?

notes: 15 cards: 7 term to definition, 4 person-or-body, 2 figure, 2 cause to effect. Tightened the three practitioner fronts (barber-surgeon, apothecary, quack) so each names a unique feature and they cannot interfere.
